messages:
elaine: quick heads-up, opened PR to add SDK helpers for coercing funcall/tool outputs across Python + Go. aim: make common schema/typing mismatches trivial (string numbers, nulls, singletons) and unify streaming retry semantics. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/438

sam: nice. question: how do you handle streaming when the funcall finishes mid-json token? we've been seeing partial chunks in prod that break naive parsers.

elaine: plan is incremental buffer-and-parse: append chunks until a top-level JSON value is parseable, then coerce+emit. pseudo:
```
buffer += chunk
if parseable_top_level_json(buffer):
    value, rest = parse_one_json(buffer)
    emit(coerce(schema, value))
    buffer = rest
else:
    continue
```
This defers emission until an entire object/array/string is available. open to concerns about latency/backpressure.

alex: buffering is reasonable. two operational notes: 1) backpressure in extremely long non-json prefixes (e.g., model hallucination) could stall streams; we should bound buffer size and surface an error. 2) retries: if the SDK retries mid-stream we must avoid duplicate emits. recommend server include a stable event id header on stream events.

nina: to formalize, propose SDK `streaming_retry_policy` with modes: "off" (no dedupe, default), "event-dedupe" (dedupe using server-provided event-id), and "idempotent" (require user idempotency token so server can filter). also add an integration test that simulates reconnect + repeated sequences.

mike: review requested. one API design: coercion helper should not drop un-coercible values silently. default = lenient (coerce common cases: "42"->42, [x] -> x, null->optional), but provide `strict=True` to raise CoercionError. tests for error payloads required.

elaine: agreed. current default is lenient; will add `strict=True|False`, CoercionError, and an example. also adding `on_coercion_failure` callback hook so callers can log or mutate.

sam: language quirk: Go's json.Unmarshal turns numbers into float64 when decoding into interface{}. the Go helper should prefer int64 for schema.integer and handle overflow/precision. add unit tests for 32/64 boundaries and negative numbers.

alex: another auth edgecase: if token refresh occurs mid-stream and SDK reconnects with a fresh token, server may replay the same logical events but chunk boundaries differ. dedupe must use event ids, not chunk fingerprints. request server to add `x-stream-event-id` per event. fallback: SDK can normalize small JSON objects and dedupe by canonical form when header missing.

elaine: added a note in PR describing the recommended server contract: include `x-stream-event-id` or `event_id` json field. also implement a fallback canonicalization function for small objects (strip whitespace, sort keys) for dedupe.

ci-bot: unit pipeline passed (unit/438) — go/json_coerce_test flaky flagged unstable on linux/amd64, rerun scheduled.

mike: can we avoid flaky tests blocking approval? add a non-flaky integration that runs without race detector and deterministic seed. also add a tiny timeout-based test to exercise buffer bounds.

elaine: adding fixup commit to stabilize tests and the integration harness. will canary the Python helper in hosted for 72h behind a feature flag, then stage to Dedicated. will post rollout steps in #eng-releases when canary starts.

sam: can you open a PERF ticket to measure latency tradeoffs of buffer timeout vs buffer-size? want numbers before we flip flags for high-throughput customers.

elaine: will file PERF ticket after merge. tagging @mike for final review when CI is green. thanks :thumbsup:
